98048577.s: Bin Salman Farm in Taif is a unique destination celebrating the region's rose and almond farming heritage. In spring it turns into a fragrant pink garden filled with the scent of authentic Taif roses. The farm has cafes and outdoor seating areas among the rose fields and the Sarawat mountain range, along with a small workshop making perfumes and soap from roses. It is known for its delicious rose cake and distinctive coffee, but booking or visiting in the early morning is advised to avoid crowds and limited parking.

98048576.s: The oldest tree in Taif, standing for more than 2,000 years in Wadi Al Wuheit, a witness to the region's history and a symbol of Saudi natural heritage. This ancient tree stands on the Al Waht and Al Wuheit tourist road in Taif. It is one of the best-known ancient trees in the Kingdom and a living witness to the region's long history. The tree is surrounded by stunning natural scenery and areas for camping and family outings, with the remains of old palm trees around it reflecting the valley's farming history. Visitors come to reflect and take photographs.

98048575.s: A mountain in Taif surrounded by dense juniper trees, where temperatures drop with altitude and visitors are rewarded with panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and valleys. Mount Daka in Taif is covered with a dense canopy of ancient juniper trees, and temperatures drop gradually as visitors climb toward the summit, making it a refreshing escape from the summer heat. The mountain offers natural trails for walking among the trees, and wide panoramic views over the surrounding valleys and plains. It is a quiet destination away from tourist crowds, suited to camping and nature photography in a relatively cool mountain atmosphere.

98048574.s: A traditional factory producing Taif rose oil and rose water, where visitors can watch the traditional distillation process in a heritage atmosphere that reflects the authenticity of this long-established craft. Rashed Al Qurashi Factory is one of the oldest rose oil and rose water factories in Taif, offering visitors the chance to watch the traditional distillation of the famous Taif rose, along with a short documentary film explaining the history of this long-established craft. The factory has a spacious shop selling luxury perfumes, rose oil and rose water at varying prices, and a quiet cafe overlooking a cool mountain setting. The entry fee is nominal, no more than 5 riyals.

98048439.s: Discover the beekeeping heritage of the Asir region, enjoy tasting a variety of natural honeys, and shop at the dedicated store in a heritage atmosphere with a unique family history. The Honey Hut Experience (Bees Tower Honey Refinery) is a unique heritage destination that introduces visitors to the history of a long-established local family famous for beekeeping and honey production across generations. The site has a building designed as towers resembling beehives, and a tasting hall displaying more than 40 different kinds of natural honey such as sidr, black seed and almond, along with a shop selling products, a cafe and a restaurant.

98048437.s: The heritage palace in Al Qazaa village is an archaeological landmark in the Asir region. It took about 140 years to build, and embodies the details of old southern architecture with its polished stones and traditional carvings. The palace was recently restored by a local artist to preserve its authentic character. It is now owned by a descendant of the founding family, who receives visitors in person and tells them the story of the palace and the family history. The place serves hot and cold drinks prepared locally in an authentic heritage atmosphere, and a visit is a rich cultural experience rather than just a sightseeing tour.

98048434.s: Enjoy Fabyland, the indoor entertainment center in Al Rashid Mall in Abha, full of games and varied activities for all ages. Fabyland is a large indoor entertainment center inside Al Rashid Mall in Abha, and one of the city's leading indoor entertainment destinations, especially on hot or rainy days. The center has a wide range of traditional and modern arcade games, along with special offers for children with disabilities that let them enjoy a suitable entertainment experience. Some of the mobile rides operate only at set evening times, so it is advisable to check operating hours in advance and to allow for crowds during holidays.

The park runs on prepaid cards that let children ride a number of rides or enter the dinosaur section separately, and has a prayer room and clean restrooms. It is a suitable place for a family evening at reasonable prices, and visiting in the evening, away from the heat of the day, is recommended.

It is advisable to use a vehicle suited to rough mountain roads when heading there, and to contact the owner in advance to confirm the booking.

98048428.s: A resort with many options for accommodation, food, drinks and events, with the largest dancing fountain in Saudi Arabia and a model of a traditional southern village. Valley Resort is located in Wadi Ibn Hashbal in the Asir region, and is one of the largest family resorts in the area, with its wide grounds and many facilities. It has the largest dancing fountain in Saudi Arabia and a miniature model of a traditional southern village, along with a farm with fruit trees and palms and areas to tour on foot, by golf cart or on double-decker buses. It offers a variety of accommodation options, restaurants and cafes, and setting aside a full day to enjoy all its facilities is recommended.

98048427.s: A natural site with seasonal waterfalls in a distinctive mountain environment, with water flow at its best during the rainy season. Al Mohatibah Waterfall is a very steep natural site in Abha, with a seasonal waterfall that flows heavily after rainfall in a rugged mountain setting with stunning scenery. Reaching the site requires great caution because the road is rough and very steep, so it is not recommended for families with children or elderly people. It is a favorite destination for adventure lovers and nature photographers, and it is best to check the weather and water level before heading there.

98048424.s: Located on a mountain top in Al Soudah, known for its stunning views and permanently misty atmosphere, with family seating and walking trails among the clouds. Al Sahab Park sits on the summit of one of the towering Al Soudah mountains and is one of the highest tourist points in the Kingdom, where visitors can literally touch the clouds as they pass through the site. The park offers wooden cabins and seating areas for rent by the hour, with local meals such as rice and chicken in reasonably priced packages. The site is very busy, especially in summer when people escape the heat, and advance booking for the seating areas and warm clothing are advised because of the cold weather at the top.

98048421.s: The Fog Walkway in Abha offers an enchanting seven-kilometer experience among the clouds and stunning scenery, with varied recreational facilities for all visitors. The Fog Walkway in Abha runs for seven kilometers along a mountain path through the clouds that cover the area most days of the year, and is one of the best-known walkways in the Kingdom. The path has several rest and photo stops with enchanting panoramic views over the surrounding valleys, along with warning signs about baboons that may occasionally appear in the area. Cafes and shops selling coffee and light snacks are spread along the walkway, with limited parking during peak times.

Tamniah Peaks Park is a high mountain site in the town of Tamniah in the Asir region, known for its stunning views stretching over the green mountains and surrounding valleys along the road leading to it. The road passes through beautiful heritage villages with traditional Asiri architecture, and the area has an enchanting misty atmosphere that lets visitors watch the clouds from the mountain top. The site currently lacks some services such as restrooms, so advance preparation before visiting is advised, along with environmental responsibility to keep nature clean.

98048385.s: A quiet green space in nature, suitable for family gatherings with stunning mountain views over the Al Habala area. Al Habala Park is one of the most thrilling destinations in the Asir region. It sits on the edge of a towering mountain overlooking the Sarawat mountain range, with an amazing panoramic view that feels like walking above the clouds. The site is known for its cable car over the valley, although its operation sometimes stops for maintenance, along with cabins and shaded seating for families and restaurants serving traditional food. The site needs a relatively long time to enjoy its facilities fully, and visitors are advised to bring a snack and be ready for cold weather even in summer.

98048382.s: A vibrant street with art galleries, theaters and upscale restaurants, famous for its purple jacaranda tree season. The Art Street in the Al Muftaha district of Abha is an open walkway that combines nature and art. It is famous worldwide for the jacaranda trees that cover the street in purple every April, when it becomes a tourist attraction visited for photography by people from across the Kingdom. The street has cafes, small restaurants and shaded seating areas, along with art galleries scattered along its sides. Visiting early in the morning is advised to avoid crowds and enjoy ideal natural light for photography.

98048379.s: Fatima Museum (the Al-Qatt Al-Aseeri Museum) is dedicated to the women's art of Al-Qatt Al-Asiri, the wall decoration art that UNESCO has inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The museum displays original examples of the bright, colorful designs that Asiri women used to decorate the walls and ceilings of their homes, along with a detailed explanation of the history and symbolism of this art. The museum offers interactive workshops where visitors learn the basics of the art themselves under the guidance of specialist women artists, and advance booking is advised because of the high demand.

Visiting in the evening is advised, when the city lights come on below the mountain in an enchanting sight, though visitors should allow for limited parking at peak times.
